summary: A row of actions — a dialog's Cancel and Confirm, a form's Back, Save and Next, a record's header actions. Owns the gap, the order and what happens when the row runs out of room.
useWhen: two or more actions sit together: a dialog or drawer footer, the end of a form, a page or card header
one action is primary and the rest are alternatives to it
the row may be narrower than its actions — a phone, a side panel — and has to wrap, stack or overflow rather than spill

useInstead.when: many controls act on one thing — a table's batch actions, an editor's formatting
useInstead.why: a toolbar is one tab stop with arrow keys inside; a ButtonGroup is a tab stop per action, which is right for two or three and tiring for ten

useInstead.when: the buttons are one choice among options, one of them selected
useInstead.why: that is a radio group with a value; a ButtonGroup holds independent actions
a group of one adds nothing

composition.note: Children in reading order, least important first, the primary last. It is drawn in that order: the primary lands at the end of the row in either direction, and last in the stack on a phone.
composition.example: <ButtonGroup stack start={<Button variant="tertiary">Back</Button>}><Button variant="secondary">Save and exit</Button><Button type="submit">Next</Button></ButtonGroup>

end.use: the default — dialog, drawer and form footers

start.use: actions under a left-aligned block of text

center.use: a centred dialog or empty state

wrap.use: the default — actions that do not fit move to a second line, all still shown

menu.use: a header row that must stay one line: the Buttons that do not fit move into More actions, first Button first; the primary and anything that is not a Button stay

children.note: the actions, primary last. With `overflow="menu"` only Buttons move, and each needs a text label or `aria-label` — it is what the menu item says

start.note: pinned to the start edge, apart from the rest — Back in a wizard, a count in a save bar. It never collapses

requires: the primary last among the children — the order is the reading, Tab and drawn order, and nothing reorders it
with `overflow="menu"`, a text label or `aria-label` on every Button that may move, and `moreLabel` translated
guarantees: every action is its own tab stop, in the order it is read; no `row-reverse`, so the drawn order never contradicts the Tab order (WCAG 2.4.3)
8px between actions, and between `start` and the rest
the order mirrors in a right-to-left locale: the primary is at the start of the line there
`stack` below 32rem of viewport: one action per line, full width, in reading order, the primary last and nearest the thumb

`overflow="menu"` keeps the row on one line and inside its box. The Buttons that do not fit move into a MenuTrigger named "More actions" at the row's start; hidden ones are out of the Tab order and the accessibility tree
a menu item presses the real Button, so its `onPress`, its `onClick` and `type="submit"` behave as if it were clicked; a disabled Button is a disabled menu item
with room again, every action comes back and More goes — also in a parent that sizes to its content, such as PageHeader's actions
notes: a menu item cannot show a Button's variant: a destructive action that must look destructive should not be allowed to overflow — make it the primary, or put it in `start`
Enter in a form submits the first submit button in the DOM order; with the primary last, give the others `type="button"` (IonBase's Button is `type="button"` unless told otherwise)

antiPatterns.why: hand-built rows each pick their own gap and none decides what happens on a phone — the demo had 8, 12 and a spacer span

antiPatterns.dont: flex-direction: row-reverse, to put the primary on the right while it comes first in the markup
antiPatterns.do: the primary last among the children
antiPatterns.why: Tab then walks the row backwards from how it is drawn, and a screen reader reads the primary before the options it is chosen over

antiPatterns.dont: <ButtonGroup overflow="menu"> around icon-only Buttons with no `aria-label`
antiPatterns.do: an `aria-label` on each, which becomes its menu item's text
antiPatterns.why: a collapsed icon-only Button has nothing to be called in the menu

antiPatterns.dont: a ButtonGroup of ten actions on one record
antiPatterns.do: <Toolbar>, or a MenuTrigger for the rare ones
antiPatterns.why: ten tab stops in a row is ten presses to get past it
